record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove that perturbations of the Schwarzschild and Kerr black-hole solutions decay, as suggested by physical and linearized arguments, thereby establishing black-hole stability in that sense?

evidence.quote: Physical and linearisation arguments suggest that a perturbation of the Schwarzscrilld (and Kerr) solution decays exponentially (black holes a:re stable); see Chandresekhar [Ch] for a comprehensive review. Prove this.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathcal{M},g_{M})$ denote the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $M>0$, and let $(\mathcal{M},g_{M,a})$ denote the Kerr spacetime of mass $M>0$ and angular momentum parameter $a$ with $|a|<M$. Both are vacuum solutions of the Einstein equations $\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$.

Consider an initial data set $(\Sigma,\bar g,K)$ for the vacuum Einstein equations consisting of a Riemannian 3-manifold $\Sigma$, a metric $\bar g$, and a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ satisfying the constraint equations, and assume that this data is a sufficiently small smooth perturbation (in a suitable weighted Sobolev norm) of the induced data on a Cauchy hypersurface of a fixed Schwarzschild (respectively Kerr) background with parameters $(M_0)$ (respectively $(M_0,a_0)$, $|a_0|<M_0$).

Prove the following nonlinear stability statement: the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of such perturbed initial data possesses a complete future null infinity $\mathcal{I}^{+}$ and an event horizon $\mathcal{H}^{+}$, and the spacetime metric asymptotically settles, in the exterior of the event horizon, to a member of the Kerr family with nearby parameters $(M_\infty,a_\infty)$, with quantitative (polynomial or exponential, in the appropriate sense) decay of the geometric quantities measuring the deviation from the limiting Kerr solution.
artifact.category_tag: Black hole stability in general relativity
artifact.status_search_result: The nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild has been established (Dafermos–Holzegel–Rodnianski–Taylor, and other works), and the nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr (|a| ≪ M) has been proved in a series of papers by Klainerman–Szeftel, Giorgi–Klainerman–Szeftel, and Shen. Linear stability of Kerr has been extended to the full subextremal range |a|<M by Shlapentokh-Rothman–Teixeira da Costa and others, but the nonlinear stability of Kerr in the full subextremal range remains open.

status_evidence.title: Kerr stability for small angular momentum
status_evidence.snippet: Klainerman and Szeftel establish the nonlinear stability of Kerr black holes for small angular momentum |a| ≪ M.
status_evidence.claim: Nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr is established.

status_evidence.title: Linear stability of Kerr black holes in the full subextremal range
status_evidence.snippet: Linear stability of the Kerr family in the full subextremal range has been proved unconditionally.
status_evidence.claim: Linear (but not yet nonlinear) stability for full subextremal Kerr is known.

status_evidence.title: Columbia Lectures on the stability of Kerr
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of progress on nonlinear stability of Kerr, restricted to small angular momentum.
status_evidence.claim: Full subextremal nonlinear Kerr stability remains an open problem.
